key_insight: Adding a hemispherical leading-edge curvature changes separation and vortex shedding, producing thicker vortical regions and an earlier shedding onset at low Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: For low-Re small UAV or aquatic vehicle blades/plates, the leading-edge shape can materially affect unsteady loads and glide performance, especially at moderate angles of attack.
method: 2D numerical simulation of a flat plate with and without hemispherical leading-edge curvature
Angle of attack sweep from 0° to 25°
Re = 1000 with comparison of vortex shedding and force coefficients
evidence_signal: The abstract reports delayed shedding for the simple flat plate, shedding onset at 5° for the curved plate, and multiple force-coefficient frequencies at higher angles.
watch_item: Results are based on 2D low-Re simulations, so 3D effects, higher-Re behavior, and manufacturing tolerances may change the observed performance.
paper_title: Effect of leading edge geometry on aerodynamic performance of a flat plate
